clue.text: Sees no Conservative wearing appropriate clothing in parliament?

indicators.note: a garment is worn around the body, so the clothing word goes round the party letter

parts.note: MPs are expected to wear neckties in the Commons; the question mark flags the playful definition

explanation.surface: Someone observes that no Tory is dressed properly in the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' puts the C inside, as if the ties had a Tory in them. The question mark admits ties are a loose definition of parliamentary dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see or spot it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bishop getting the sack after upsetting article's seized

indicators.note: after puts the bishop and sack pieces behind the article
upsetting means overturning, so the article is written backwards in a down clue

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A bishop is sent to bed after upsetting an article, then grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabbed is informal for caught or grabbed, a synonym of seized.

clue.text: Some feminists' poor theory about men

indicators.note: about means turning around, so the run is read backwards
some means only part of these words is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Some feminists have a weak theory about men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SPOORT from inside the words; 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are soldiers, and men is a common military term for the rank and file.

clue.text: Contrast MP in Cairo cavorting with relative

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A British politician frolicking in Cairo alongside a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparison weighs one thing against another, so it is a near-synonym of a contrast.

clue.text: Father close to an alluring woman

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent

indicators.note: close to means the end of the next word, its final letter

explanation.surface: A father getting close to an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Sirens lured sailors with song, so the word means a seductive temptress.

clue.text: Hold me back — get ready!

indicators.note: back here means the little word me is turned round, read from right to left

parts.note: to brace yourself is to prepare for an impact

explanation.surface: A cry to a partner: hug me in return, and brace yourself!
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, a holding of someone in your arms, so the noun matches hold.

clue.text: European cross and worried — that's priceless

parts.note: X is shaped like a cross
pensive means thoughtful in an anxious way

explanation.surface: A European angry and worried about something hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the letter X. 'Priceless' looks like hilarious, but here it is costing a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priceless costs more than can be reckoned, so it is very costly.

clue.text: Blunder, whichever way you look at it

definitions.note: British slang for a silly mistake

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading the word top to bottom or bottom to top gives the same letters

parts.note: British slang for a silly mistake

explanation.surface: A gaffe that looks bad from any angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom, normally meaning 'however you consider it', here says the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a silly mistake, a synonym of blunder.

clue.text: Place for croaking animals?

parts.note: croaking is slang for dying, so a place where livestock meet their end; the surface suggests a frog pond

explanation.surface: A pond where frogs croak.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where livestock are killed, the place animals go to die.

clue.text: Half of gemstones by cove suddenly appearing

indicators.note: half of means only the first four of the eight letters are kept

parts.note: emeralds are green gemstones
cove is old British slang for a man, a gent

explanation.surface: Half the gems are found beside a cove, suddenly coming into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' looks like a bay; it is old slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent describes something coming into being or view, just beginning to appear.

clue.text: Do very well as Liberal in time of prosperity

indicators.note: in places the party letter within the word for a period of prosperity

parts.note: an economic boom is a time of prosperity

explanation.surface: A Liberal party thriving during an economic boom.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to flourish or thrive, an idiom for doing very well.

clue.text: Religious education document that's about will corrupt

parts.note: RE is the British school subject Religious Education
probate is the official certificate that proves a will

explanation.surface: A legal paper about someone's will that will corrupt religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the testament that probate concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is a depraved, unprincipled person; as an adjective it means morally rotten, like corrupt.

clue.text: Describing former lover: unattractive, independent and no good

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
plain means homely, not good-looking

explanation.surface: Someone describes a former partner as plain, independent and worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Explaining something means setting it out in words, which is a near-synonym of describing.

clue.text: Animal's leg cut

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, its final letter docked

parts.note: a leg of a journey is one stage of it

explanation.surface: An animal's leg that has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Trip Laura organised without Charlie for certain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the C
organised means arranged into a new order

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trip Laura arranged without Charlie, for sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: the anagram of TRIP LAURA goes round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular and certain both pick out a specific one, as in a particular day or a certain day.

clue.text: Work of civilian — it's getting flak

indicators.note: work here means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: only the it is used; the apostrophe s stands for is, joining fodder to the definition

explanation.surface: A civilian's work is coming under criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges OF CIVILIAN IT. 'Work of' looks like a phrase, but 'of' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is harsh criticism, and vilification is abusive disparagement, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: The same model conceals new facial twitch

indicators.note: conceals means the model word hides the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ideal is a perfect model to follow
a tic is an involuntary twitch, often of the face

explanation.surface: A fashion model is hiding a fresh facial twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person posing; it is an ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things are exactly alike, which is what the same means.

clue.text: Rocks suit

definitions.meaning: rocks is slang for gems, especially precious cut stones
one of the four card suits, with hearts, clubs and spades

explanation.definitionFit: The gemstones are slang rocks, and the red card suit shares the name.

clue.text: American pressure on Macron's little demand

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
petite is French for little; Emmanuel Macron is the French president

explanation.surface: American pressure falls on the French president's small request.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite as in market appetite is a desire for something, the economic sense of demand.

clue.text: I prevent mom's tipsy advances

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stops their tipsy mother's advances.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvements are steps forward, progress, the plural noun sense of advances.

clue.text: A piece of cake in mess — I'm pleased!

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside these words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone happy despite a slice of cake landing in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something easy, which is what simple means.

clue.text: May not initially hiding information about business

indicators.note: hiding means the shortened month word encloses the other pieces
not initially means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone may not be hiding information about a company at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' takes M from MAY, leaving AY, which holds GEN and C.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm providing a service, such as a travel agency, so a kind of business.

clue.text: Come face to face with turkey, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, spoken rather than written

parts.note: turkey is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: Encountering a turkey, perhaps at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to encounter them in person, an idiom for coming face to face.

clue.text: Pulling out twine wrapped around chisel?

indicators.note: wrapped around means the twine word encloses the tool word

parts.note: twine is string
to etch is to cut a design into metal; the question mark admits chisel is a loose synonym

explanation.surface: Twine is being pulled out and wound around a chisel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretching something means drawing it out longer, the same as pulling it out.

clue.text: Peter out with student getting artist's equipment

parts.note: to ease off is to lessen or die down, as things peter out
L is for learner, from the British learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A student's enthusiasm petering out once given painting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter rests the canvas on a wooden stand, so it is a piece of artist's kit.

clue.text: Wise men showing endless charm

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: magic is a charm or spell

explanation.surface: Wise men displaying an infinite charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Wise Men of the Nativity story are traditionally called the Magi.

clue.text: Drunk causes inn problems

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drunkard creates trouble at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuisances are annoyances or troubles, plural nouns matching problems.

clue.text: 9 large heads of universities peckish immediately before noon

indicators.note: heads of means the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A list of big university heads feeling hungry just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' refers to the answer to 9 across, BLOOM, so the definition is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A lupin is a tall garden plant with spikes of flowers, an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Amateur records flipping exceptional

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: laic means lay, non-professional, as an amateur is
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: An amateur flips through records, finding something exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: Something special is out of the ordinary, which is what exceptional means.

clue.text: King on board galley, drifting in the main

indicators.note: on board means the king letter is placed inside the ship's letters
drifting suggests the ship's letters wander out of order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A king aboard a galley drifting on the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drifting' rearranges GALLEY into LAGELY; R goes inside. 'The main' is also an old word for the sea, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely means for the most part, mostly, which is the idiom in the main.
